api_function: Retrieve Ensembl VEP-based annotations for a provided list of genomic variants. The endpoint accepts a JSON array of variant identifiers in genomic HGVS (HGVSg) format (GRCh37 or GRCh38) and returns, per variant, effect predictions and rich annotations (e.g., transcript consequences, hotspots, Mutation Assessor, MyVariant.info, OncoKB, nucleotide context, PTMs, signal annotations). Optional query parameters allow specifying an isoform override source, supplying API tokens for licensed data sources, and restricting the response to specific annotation sections.
parameters_constraints: Request body (application/json) is required and must be a JSON array of strings, each a valid genomic HGVS (HGVSg) representation on GRCh37 or GRCh38 (e.g., "X:g.66937331T>A", "17:g.41242962_41242963insGA", "3:g.319781del", "19:g.110753dup"). Each variant string should use chromosome labels 1–22, X, or Y; 1-based integer coordinates; and proper syntax for SNVs (Ref>Alt with A/C/G/T), insertions (ins), deletions (del, optionally with ranges), or duplications (dup). Avoid whitespace and ensure consistent genome build per workflow. Query parameter isoformOverrideSource (optional, string): a non-empty name of a supported isoform override source (e.g., "uniprot"); unsupported values may be ignored or rejected. Query parameter token (optional, string): must be a valid JSON object encoded as a string and URL-encoded when placed in the query, mapping source names to access tokens (e.g., {"source1":"token1","source2":"token2"}); keys and values should be non-empty strings. Query parameter fields (optional, array of strings): a case-sensitive list of annotation section names to include; can be provided as a comma-separated list or as repeated parameters depending on client behavior; each item must match a supported field name (e.g., hotspots, oncokb, mutation_assessor, my_variant_info, nucleotide_context, ptms, signalAnnotation). If omitted, default behavior applies (the implementation may include a default such as "hotspots").

api_function: Retrieves VEP (Variant Effect Predictor) annotations and related variant metadata for a provided list of dbSNP identifiers (rsIDs). For each rsID, the service can return transcript consequence summaries, genomic locations, ClinVar/gnomAD/MyVariantInfo/OncoKB signals, protein-level effects, and other integrated resources. Optional query parameters let clients specify an isoform override source (e.g., uniprot), pass per-source access tokens, and restrict the response to selected fields.
parameters_constraints:
- Request body (application/json, required): must be a JSON array of strings, each string a dbSNP identifier in the form rs followed by digits (e.g., "rs116035550"). Provide one or more valid rsIDs; the body must be valid JSON and encoded as UTF-8.
- fields (query, optional): a list of field names to include in the response; values are case-sensitive and must match valid response property names (e.g., annotation_summary). May be supplied as a comma-separated string or as repeated query parameters, depending on client encoding. Unknown or misspelled fields will not be returned.
- isoformOverrideSource (query, optional): a non-empty string naming a supported isoform override source (for example, "uniprot"). The value should match a source recognized by the service; omit to use default behavior.
- token (query, optional): a stringified JSON object mapping source names to access tokens, for example {"source1":"token1","source2":"token2"}. It must be valid JSON when decoded from the query string and URL-encoded when sent; keys and values should be non-empty strings.
- General: query parameters must be URL-encoded; if input rsIDs are invalid or fields do not match available properties, the service may return an error or an empty/partial result.

api_function: Retrieve Ensembl VEP-based annotation for a variant identified by a dbSNP rsID. The endpoint aggregates core VEP annotations (e.g., allele string, genomic location, most severe consequence, transcript consequences and intergenic consequences) and may include additional sources such as ClinVar, gnomAD (exome/genome), MyVariant.info, COSMIC, MutationAssessor, nucleotide context, hotspots, PTMs, and OncoKB clinical interpretations (when a valid token is supplied). Optional query parameters let clients choose an isoform override source and limit the response to specific fields.
parameters_constraints: variantId (path, required): must be a valid dbSNP identifier in the form 'rs' followed by digits (e.g., rs116035550); no whitespace or trailing punctuation. isoformOverrideSource (query, optional): a single string naming a supported isoform override source; commonly 'uniprot'. Values are limited to sources supported by the service, and unrecognized values may be ignored or cause the default behavior to be used. token (query, optional): although typed as string, it should contain a JSON object serialized to a string mapping data source names to their API tokens (e.g., {"oncokb":"<token>"}); must be valid JSON when parsed server-side and URL-encoded when sent as a query parameter. fields (query, optional): a comma-separated list of case-sensitive field names to include in the response; each value must exactly match available top-level response properties (e.g., annotation_summary, intergenic_consequences, transcript_consequences, clinvar, my_variant_info, gnomadExome, gnomadGenome, oncokb, nucleotide_context, hotspots, ptms, start, end, strand, most_severe_consequence, id, variant). Unknown or mis-cased names will not match and may be omitted or rejected depending on server behavior. If omitted, the service returns its default set of fields (often including annotation_summary).

api_function: Retrieve Ensembl VEP-based functional annotations for a provided list of genomic locations (chromosome, start, end, reference allele, variant allele). This batch endpoint accepts multiple loci and returns transcript consequences and rich variant context such as most severe consequence, ClinVar/COSMIC/gnomAD data, Ensembl mappings, protein-level predictions (SIFT/PolyPhen), and optional sections like hotspots, PTMs, nucleotide context, OncoKB clinical interpretations, and related signals—useful for annotating VCF/MAF variants in bioinformatics workflows.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required, must use application/json, and must be an array of objects; each object must include the case-sensitive properties chromosome (string), start (int32), end (int32), referenceAllele (string), and variantAllele (string). chromosome must be a valid reference contig name for the assembly (e.g., 1–22, X, Y, MT); start and end must be positive 32-bit integers (numeric, not quoted); referenceAllele and variantAllele must be non-empty DNA sequences composed of valid bases (A, C, G, T; N allowed; multi-base strings permitted for indels). Query parameter isoformOverrideSource is optional and must be a non-empty string naming a supported isoform source (e.g., uniprot). Query parameter token is optional and must be a well-formed JSON object encoded as a string that maps source names to their access tokens (e.g., {"source":"token"}); ensure it is URL-encoded when placed in the query string. Query parameter fields is optional and represents an array of case-sensitive section names to include; it may be supplied as a single comma-separated list or as repeated fields parameters (form style, explode=true). Each value should be a supported section such as hotspots, clinvar, my_variant_info, mutation_assessor, oncokb, nucleotide_context, ptms, or signalAnnotation.

api_function: Retrieve Ensembl VEP-based annotation for a specific genomic locus and allele change. Given a genomic location (chromosome, start, end, reference allele, alternate allele), the API returns a comprehensive variant annotation including consequence predictions and optional data blocks (e.g., hotspots, OncoKB, ClinVar, MyVariant.info, gnomAD, nucleotide context, PTMs, and other sections).
parameters_constraints: genomicLocation (path, required): Must be a single string formatted as chromosome,start,end,referenceAllele,alternateAllele with commas as separators and no spaces. Chromosome should be a valid reference contig (typically 1–22, X, Y, MT/M); coordinates are 1-based positive integers; start must be <= end; alleles should be DNA bases using uppercase letters (A, C, G, T; N may be accepted). For single-nucleotide variants, start equals end; for indels, ref/alt lengths may differ. isoformOverrideSource (query, optional): A non-empty string naming a supported isoform source (e.g., uniprot); use the exact identifier expected by the service. token (query, optional): A string containing a JSON object that maps source names to their access tokens (e.g., provider-to-token map). It must be valid JSON and properly URL-encoded when sent in the query string. fields (query, optional): List of field identifiers to include; values are case-sensitive. Provided as an array of strings (can be passed as multiple fields parameters or as a comma-separated list depending on client), each item must match a recognized section name such as hotspots, oncokb, my_variant_info, mutation_assessor, nucleotide_context, ptms, signalAnnotation, clinvar, colocatedVariants. Unrecognized names may be ignored or rejected by the service.

api_function: Retrieve Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) annotation for a specific genomic variant. The endpoint returns detailed consequence and mapping information (e.g., transcript consequences, genomic location, HGVS strings), and can include optional sources such as hotspots, ClinVar, COSMIC, gnomAD, OncoKB, nucleotide context, PTMs, and signal annotations to support bioinformatics workflows involving MAF/VCF variant annotation and enrichment with Ensembl/PFAM/PDB-related data.
parameters_constraints: variant (path, required): must be a non-empty string representing a single genomic variant in a recognized HGVS-like genomic format (e.g., chr:g.start[_end]{>ALT|del|insALT|dup} such as 17:g.41242962_41242963insGA). Use valid chromosome identifiers and 1-based coordinates; no whitespace; URL-encode if special characters are present. isoformOverrideSource (query, optional): free-text source identifier for isoform/canonical transcript overrides and must match a supported source (e.g., uniprot); unsupported values may be ignored. token (query, optional): a JSON object serialized as a string mapping data source names to access tokens (e.g., {"source1":"token1","source2":"token2"}); it must be valid JSON and URL-encoded in the query; invalid or missing tokens may prevent licensed/limited fields from being returned. fields (query, optional): list of field names to include; values are case-sensitive and must match supported top-level annotation sections (e.g., hotspots, oncokb, ptms, nucleotide_context, signalAnnotation, clinvar). The API may accept either a comma-separated single parameter (fields=hotspots,oncokb) or repeated parameters (fields=hotspots&fields=oncokb) depending on client encoding; unrecognized field names will not be returned.

api_function: Accepts a list of NCBI Entrez Gene IDs and returns, for each, the canonical Ensembl Gene ID along with the approved HUGO symbol and related synonyms. This endpoint supports genomic annotation workflows by mapping Entrez identifiers to canonical Ensembl gene records.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing a JSON array. Each array element must be a string representing a valid NCBI Entrez Gene ID. Each ID string should be non-empty and composed only of decimal digits (0–9), with no signs, decimals, whitespace, or prefixes (e.g., do not include 'GeneID:' or Ensembl-style prefixes such as 'ENSG'). Do not supply gene symbols or Ensembl IDs; the endpoint specifically expects Entrez Gene IDs. Ensure the payload is a well-formed JSON array of strings; nulls, objects, numbers, and empty strings are not valid items.

api_function: Given an NCBI Entrez Gene ID, this endpoint returns the corresponding canonical Ensembl gene identifier along with gene metadata such as the approved HGNC symbol, synonyms, and previous symbols. It is used to map an Entrez Gene ID to its canonical Ensembl gene record for downstream genomic annotation workflows.
parameters_constraints: Path parameter entrezGeneId is required and must represent a valid NCBI Entrez Gene identifier. Although defined as a string in the schema, its semantic constraint is a positive integer composed only of digits (e.g., 23140), with no signs, spaces, decimal points, or prefixes (do not include labels like 'ENTREZ:' or 'GeneID:'). It must be non-empty and URL-safe (digits need no encoding). The value should correspond to an existing Entrez Gene ID recognized by the service to successfully resolve a canonical Ensembl gene.

api_function: Batch lookup of canonical Ensembl Gene IDs from a list of HGNC-approved gene symbols (HUGO symbols). For each provided symbol, the API returns the corresponding Ensembl gene ID and the approved symbol, and may include additional metadata such as synonyms, previous symbols, and Entrez Gene ID. This is useful for mapping gene symbols to Ensembl identifiers in genomic variant annotation workflows.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be sent as application/json. It must be a JSON array where each item is a non-empty string representing a single HGNC-approved gene symbol (e.g., "TP53", "PIK3CA", "BRCA1"). Each element must be a string (not null, number, or object). Symbols should correspond to official HGNC-approved gene symbols; unrecognized or invalid symbols may not yield a mapping. While not strictly enforced by the schema, providing unique symbols avoids duplicate results. No additional fields are accepted outside the array.

api_function: Retrieve the canonical Ensembl gene identifier for a given HGNC/HUGO gene symbol, along with the approved symbol and optional metadata such as synonyms, previous symbols, and the Entrez Gene ID. This helps genomic annotation workflows resolve human gene symbols to stable Ensembl gene IDs.
parameters_constraints: The path parameter hugoSymbol is required and must be a non-empty string representing an approved HGNC (HUGO) gene symbol (e.g., TP53). It should match an official human gene symbol rather than transcript or protein identifiers (avoid versions like TP53-001 or isoform labels). Symbols are typically uppercase and may include digits and hyphens (e.g., HLA-DRA); avoid spaces and special characters. Because it is a path parameter, any reserved or non-URL-safe characters must be percent-encoded and leading/trailing whitespace should be removed. Providing an unrecognized or improperly formatted symbol will not yield a canonical Ensembl gene ID.

api_function: Retrieve Ensembl canonical transcript information for a list of genes specified by HGNC (HUGO) gene symbols. For each provided symbol, the API returns the canonical Ensembl transcript, gene and protein IDs, and related annotations such as Pfam domains, exon/UTR structure, and optional identifiers (e.g., RefSeq mRNA, CCDS). An optional isoform override source (defaulting to "uniprot") can be used to influence canonical isoform selection.
parameters_constraints: Query parameter isoformOverrideSource: optional string in the query. If omitted, defaults to "uniprot". It should name a supported isoform-override data source (e.g., "uniprot"); provide a non-empty string without surrounding whitespace. Request body: required application/json payload. Must be a JSON array whose items are strings, each representing a valid HGNC (HUGO) gene symbol (e.g., TP53, PIK3CA, BRCA1). Avoid nulls, empty strings, or whitespace-only entries. Use official HGNC symbols (typically uppercase alphanumeric, sometimes with hyphens). The array should contain one or more symbols to yield results.

api_function: Retrieves the Ensembl canonical transcript for a given HGNC (HUGO) gene symbol, optionally using a specified isoform-override source (default: UniProt) to determine the canonical isoform. The response includes Ensembl gene/transcript/protein IDs, UniProt ID, protein length, Pfam domains, exon and UTR coordinates with strand, and common IDs such as RefSeq mRNA and CCDS.
parameters_constraints: hugoSymbol (path, required): must be a non-empty string representing a valid HGNC-approved human gene symbol (e.g., TP53). Typically uppercase ASCII letters and digits, sometimes with hyphens; no whitespace. Because it is a path segment, it must be URL-safe/URL-encoded if it contains special characters. isoformOverrideSource (query, optional): string indicating the isoform override source used to choose the canonical transcript; if omitted, defaults to 'uniprot'. It should be one of the sources supported by the service (e.g., 'uniprot'); use lowercase to match examples. Unsupported values may yield no result or a non-canonical selection.

api_function: Retrieve Ensembl transcript records. When provided with an Ensembl gene ID, an Ensembl protein ID, or a HUGO gene symbol, the API returns the transcripts that map to those identifiers along with rich annotations (e.g., transcriptId, geneId, proteinId, UniProt ID, protein length, PFAM domains, exon coordinates/ranks/strands, and UTR segments). If no query parameters are supplied, it returns all available transcripts.
parameters_constraints: All query parameters are optional and are single string values. geneId must be an Ensembl gene stable ID string that starts with the prefix 'ENSG' followed by digits only (no version suffixes or whitespace; case should be uppercase as in Ensembl IDs). proteinId must be an Ensembl protein stable ID string that starts with the prefix 'ENSP' followed by digits only (no version suffixes or whitespace; uppercase). hugoSymbol must be a valid HUGO/HGNC gene symbol (typically uppercase letters and digits, no spaces; for example, ARF5). Do not supply empty strings; omit a parameter if not used. Values should correspond to existing records in the respective nomenclatures to yield results.

api_function: Retrieves Ensembl transcript records by filtering on one identifier type: Ensembl transcript IDs, HGNC (HUGO) gene symbols, Ensembl protein IDs, or Ensembl gene IDs. The response provides transcript-centric annotations, including transcriptId, geneId, proteinId, protein length, Pfam domain intervals, exon structures (IDs, start/end, rank, strand, version), UTR intervals, and optional cross-references such as UniProt ID, RefSeq mRNA ID, CCDS ID, and associated HUGO symbols.
parameters_constraints: Request body must be application/json with an object that may include any of these array fields: geneIds, hugoSymbols, proteinIds, transcriptIds. For each field, when present: (1) transcriptIds: array of strings; each string must be a valid Ensembl transcript ID, typically starting with 'ENST' followed by digits (e.g., ENST00000361390), optionally with a version suffix (e.g., ENST00000361390.2); uppercase and no whitespace. (2) geneIds: array of strings; each string must be a valid Ensembl gene ID, starting with 'ENSG' followed by digits (e.g., ENSG00000136999), optionally with a version suffix; uppercase and no whitespace. (3) proteinIds: array of strings; each string must be a valid Ensembl protein ID, starting with 'ENSP' followed by digits (e.g., ENSP00000439985), optionally with a version suffix; uppercase and no whitespace. (4) hugoSymbols: array of strings; each string must be a valid HGNC gene symbol (HUGO), typically uppercase letters and digits and may include hyphens (e.g., TP53, PIK3CA, BRCA1, HLA-A); avoid surrounding whitespace. Each provided array should be non-empty and contain only the identifier type appropriate for that field.

api_function: Retrieve a transcript record by its Ensembl transcript ID and return detailed annotation and cross-references for bioinformatics use. The response includes the transcriptId, linked geneId and proteinId, optional UniProt ID, protein length, Pfam domain annotations (with IDs and amino-acid start/end), HUGO gene symbols, RefSeq mRNA ID, CCDS ID, exon structures (IDs, genomic start/end, rank, strand, version), and UTR regions (type, start/end, strand). This is useful for genomic variant annotation workflows that need Ensembl mappings, domain context, and related identifiers.
parameters_constraints: transcriptId (path): required, non-empty string. Must be a valid Ensembl transcript stable ID. Expected format is the uppercase prefix 'ENST' followed by exactly 11 digits (e.g., ENST00000361390). A version suffix may appear as a dot followed by one or more digits (e.g., ENST00000361390.3). The value is case-sensitive and should not contain whitespace or characters other than the allowed pattern (ENST + digits, optional '.' + digits). As a path parameter, it must not include slashes and should be URL-safe.

api_function: Looks up a single Ensembl gene stable identifier and returns its external cross-references across other databases. Given an Ensembl gene ID (e.g., ENSG00000169083), it responds with an array of xref records that include database display name, database name, primary external ID, display ID, description, version, and optional fields such as synonyms, info text/type, and the Ensembl gene ID. This supports bioinformatics workflows by mapping Ensembl genes to external resources (e.g., pathway, protein, or disease databases).
parameters_constraints: Query parameter accession is required and must be a single Ensembl gene stable identifier. It must be a non-empty ASCII string in the canonical Ensembl gene format: the exact uppercase prefix 'ENSG' followed immediately by an 11-digit zero-padded number (total length 15 characters, e.g., ENSG00000169083). Only gene IDs are accepted (transcript/protein IDs like ENST/ENSP are not valid here). The value should contain only alphanumeric characters with no spaces, punctuation, or version suffix (e.g., no '.1'). Provide exactly one accession per request; multiple values are not supported.

api_function: Bulk-retrieves PDB header metadata for a given list of PDB identifiers. For each requested PDB ID, the service returns header fields such as pdbId, title, and optional compound and source sections, enabling workflows to pull basic PDB structure information for downstream genomic/structural annotation.
parameters_constraints: Request body (named pdbIds) is required and must be sent as application/json containing an array of strings. Each array element must be a valid PDB identifier: exactly 4 alphanumeric characters (letters A–Z and digits 0–9), case-insensitive (e.g., "1a37", "1A4O"); avoid leading/trailing whitespace or any punctuation. Nulls, empty strings, and non-string values are not allowed. The array itself should not be null; provide at least one PDB ID to receive results. Duplicates may lead to redundant results and should be avoided.

api_function: Retrieve the Protein Data Bank (PDB) header metadata for a given PDB entry. On success, it returns JSON including the PDB identifier (pdbId) and the structure title, with optional compound and source metadata. This is useful in bioinformatics workflows to link annotated variants to corresponding PDB structure context.
parameters_constraints: The path parameter pdbId is required and must be a valid PDB accession code. It must be a non-empty string of exactly four characters matching the pattern ^[0-9][A-Za-z0-9]{3}$ (first character is a digit, followed by three alphanumeric characters). Letters may be upper or lower case; avoid including chain identifiers, residue numbers, or file extensions (e.g., do not append '.pdb' or ':A'). No whitespace or special characters are allowed, and since it is a path segment it must be URL-safe. Example of a valid value: '1a37'.

api_function: Accepts a JSON array of PFAM domain accession IDs and returns PFAM domain records for those accessions, including the domain name, accession, and description. This supports bioinformatics workflows by fetching protein domain information (PFAM) relevant to genomic variant annotation.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing a JSON array of strings. Each element must be a PFAM domain accession ID in the canonical format: the uppercase prefix "PF" followed by exactly five digits (e.g., PF00093, PF02827, PF15276); leading zeros are allowed. Each string should contain only the two letters and five digits (no extra whitespace or characters), and must not be null or empty. The array should be provided (non-missing) and should contain valid accession strings; accessions that do not exist in PFAM will simply not yield matching domain records in the response.

api_function: Retrieves a PFAM protein domain record by its PFAM accession identifier and returns the domain’s metadata (at least name, accession, and description). This is useful in genomic/variant annotation workflows to map variants to protein domain information.
parameters_constraints: pfamAccession is a required path parameter and must be a non-empty string representing a valid PFAM domain accession. PFAM domain accessions follow the pattern 'PF' followed by exactly five digits (total length 7; e.g., PF02827). It should be uppercase, contain only the prefix 'PF' and digits 0–9 (no spaces or additional characters), and correspond to an existing PFAM domain; otherwise the lookup will not return a domain record.

api_function: Retrieve experimentally supported post-translational modification (PTM) annotations for a single Ensembl Transcript ID. The endpoint returns an array of PTM records including the modification type, amino-acid position in the protein sequence, the protein sequence context, supporting PubMed IDs, and mappings to UniProt (accession and entry). This is useful for genomic/proteomic annotation workflows that link transcripts to protein-level PTM evidence.
parameters_constraints: Query parameter ensemblTranscriptId must be provided as a non-empty string representing a valid Ensembl Transcript ID. It should follow the canonical Ensembl transcript format, typically starting with the uppercase prefix 'ENST' followed by 11 digits (e.g., ENST00000646891), with no whitespace or version suffix (e.g., '.1'). Only a single ID is accepted per request; multiple IDs are not supported in this parameter.

api_function: Retrieves experimentally supported post‑translational modification (PTM) entries associated with the provided Ensembl transcript IDs, returning PTM details such as position, type, sequence context, UniProt accession/entry, linked Ensembl transcript IDs, and supporting PubMed IDs.
parameters_constraints: Request body is required and must be application/json containing an object with a required field transcriptIds. transcriptIds must be an array of one or more strings. Each element must be a valid Ensembl Transcript stable ID: the literal uppercase prefix 'ENST' followed by exactly 11 digits (e.g., ENST00000371953). Do not supply other Ensembl ID types (e.g., ENSG, ENSP) and avoid version suffixes (e.g., '.2'). Strings must be non-empty, free of leading/trailing whitespace, and case-sensitive (use uppercase 'ENST'). Nulls or non-string items are not allowed.

api_function: Retrieves the current Genome Nexus service version as a JSON object, allowing clients and workflows in genomic variant annotation to verify the running API version for compatibility and provenance tracking.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any input parameters (no path, query, or request body fields). Invoke it with an HTTP GET request to /version; the response will be a JSON object containing a single string field named "version".
